regionNote: UF/IFAS Central Florida is the section between State Road 40 and State Road 70. ZIP 32927 is in that band, in Brevard County.

zone.source: PRISM Group ZIP listing published for the 2023 USDA map

frostNote: UF/IFAS says frosts and freezes occur occasionally in Central Florida. The zone is the average coldest night, not a frost date and not a promise of a harvest.
disclaimer: Informational notes from public extension calendars. A listed plant can still fail. This is not a nursery.

sources.title: Growing Strawberries in the Florida Home Garden, HS403
UF/IFAS Home Citrus: Selecting a Citrus Tree

seasons.label: Cool season
seasons.hint: October is the Central Florida cool-season planting month

seasons.label: Warm season
seasons.hint: March is when the calendar names beans, peppers, tomatoes, squash, and eggplant

seasons.label: Summer
seasons.hint: June is okra, southern peas, and sweet potato

crops.name: Arugula
crops.types: Speedy, Astro.

crops.name: Bush beans
crops.types: Snap: Roma II, Provider, Contender, Bush Blue Lake. Shell types include pinto and navy.

crops.name: Pole beans
crops.types: Kentucky Wonder, McCaslan, Rattlesnake, Blue Lake.

crops.name: Lima beans
crops.types: Fordhook 242, Henderson, Jackson Wonder. Bush and pole types both exist.

crops.name: Beets
crops.types: Detroit Dark Red, Early Wonder, Cylindra, Chioggia. Leaves are edible.

crops.name: Broccoli
crops.types: Packman, De Cicco, Waltham. Broccoli raab is a different plant.

crops.name: Brussels sprouts
crops.types: Jade Cross, Long Island Improved.

crops.name: Cabbage
crops.types: Rio Verde, Copenhagen Market, Savoy, Red Acre.

crops.name: Cantaloupe
crops.types: Athena, Ambrosia, Galia.

crops.name: Carrots
crops.types: Imperator, Nantes, Danvers, Chantenay.

crops.name: Cauliflower
crops.types: Snowball strains, Snow Crown.

crops.name: Celery
crops.types: Utah strains.

crops.name: Chinese cabbage
crops.types: Heading: Napa, Michihili. Open-leaf: bok choy.

crops.name: Collards
crops.types: Georgia Southern, Top Bunch, Vates.

crops.name: Sweet corn
crops.types: Silver Queen, How Sweet It Is, Early Sunglow. Plant in a block so it pollinates.

crops.name: Cucumbers
crops.types: Slicers: Poinsett, Sweet Success. Picklers: Eureka, Boston Pickling.

crops.name: Eggplant
crops.types: Black Beauty, Dusky, Ichiban, Cloud Nine.

crops.name: Endive and escarole
crops.types: Endive: Green Curled Ruffec. Escarole: Batavian.

crops.name: Kale
crops.types: Vates, Dwarf Blue Curled, Tuscan (lacinato).

crops.name: Kohlrabi
crops.types: Early White Vienna, Early Purple Vienna.

crops.name: Lettuce
crops.types: Leaf and romaine do best: Black Seeded Simpson, Red Sails, Parris Island. Crisphead only in the coolest months.

crops.name: Mustard
crops.types: Southern Giant Curled, Florida Broad Leaf, Mizuna.

crops.name: Okra
crops.types: Clemson Spineless, Annie Oakley II, Cajun Delight.

crops.name: Bulbing onions
crops.types: Short-day Granex, yellow or white.

crops.name: Bunching onions and shallots
crops.types: Evergreen Bunching, White Lisbon, shallots. Leek: American Flag.

crops.name: English or snow peas
crops.types: Wando, Green Arrow, Sugar Snap, Oregon Sugarpod II.

crops.name: Southern peas
crops.types: California Blackeye No. 5, Pinkeye Purple Hull, Texas Cream.

crops.name: Peppers
crops.types: Sweet: California Wonder, Red Knight, Big Bertha, Cubanelle. Hot: jalapeño, Anaheim, cayenne, habanero.

crops.name: Irish potatoes
crops.types: Red Pontiac, Yukon Gold, Gold Rush. Start from certified seed pieces, not grocery potatoes.

crops.name: Sweet potatoes
crops.types: Beauregard, Centennial, Vardaman. Dry-flesh type: boniato.

crops.name: Pumpkin
crops.types: Jack O Lantern types, Jack Be Little, and tropical Seminole or calabaza.

crops.name: Radish
crops.types: Cherry Belle, White Icicle, Sparkler. Winter type: Daikon.

crops.name: Spinach
crops.types: Melody, Bloomsdale Longstanding, Tyee. For warm months the guide points to New Zealand or Malabar spinach instead.

crops.name: Summer squash
crops.types: Straightneck, crookneck, zucchini such as Black Beauty or Cocozelle.

crops.name: Winter squash
crops.types: Acorn (Table Queen), butternut (Waltham), spaghetti.

crops.name: Strawberry
crops.types: Central and south: Sweet Sensation Florida127, Florida Brilliance, Medallion, Ember, Encore. HS403 says Camarosa has been the productive one in North Florida, not Central.

crops.name: Swiss chard
crops.types: Bright Lights, Fordhook Giant, Lucullus.

crops.name: Tomatoes
crops.types: Slicing: Celebrity, Better Boy, Tasti-Lee. Cherry and grape: Sweet 100, Juliet, Sun Gold. Some BHN lines are listed as TSWV-resistant.

crops.name: Turnips
crops.types: Purple Top White Globe for roots. Seven Top and Shogoin for greens.

crops.name: Watermelon
crops.types: Jubilee, Crimson Sweet, Sugar Baby, Mickeylee.

crops.name: Calabaza
crops.note: Named for June in the Central Florida Gardening Calendar.
crops.types: Tropical pumpkin. Also listed with Seminole among UF pumpkin varieties.

crops.name: Malabar spinach
crops.note: Named for June in the Central Florida Gardening Calendar. Not true spinach.
crops.types: A warm-season green. It is not true spinach.

crops.name: Basil
crops.note: Pinch back so they branch instead of flowering.

crops.name: Mexican tarragon
crops.note: Pinch back so they branch instead of flowering.

crops.name: Rosemary
crops.note: Pinch back so they branch instead of flowering.

crops.name: Herbs from small plants
crops.note: July is too hot to start herbs from seed. Small plants can still go in.

crops.name: Fig
crops.note: Bare-root in late winter or early spring. Container plants can go in any month. Figs are grown in central Florida.
crops.types: Central Florida: Celeste, Brown Turkey (not California Brown Turkey), Green Ischia, Alma, Magnolia, San Piero.

crops.name: Citrus
crops.note: July through October is the best planting window in Florida.
crops.types: Oranges Hamlin, Valencia, and OLL-8; mandarin SugarBelle; grapefruit Duncan, Marsh, and Flame. Meyer lemon and kumquat take more cold. Tahiti and Key lime are listed for south Florida. SugarBelle and OLL-8 are the HLB-tolerant picks named in the dooryard guide; every variety can still get greening.

crops.name: Low-chill apple
crops.note: January, with the other temperate fruit trees.
crops.types: Anna, Dorsett Golden, TropicSweet. These need a pollenizer.

crops.name: Southern highbush blueberry
crops.note: January. Rabbiteye types in the same guide are listed for north Florida.
crops.types: Emerald, Jewel, Farthing, Meadowlark. Plant more than one variety.

crops.name: Muscadine grape
crops.note: January. Bunch grapes for central Florida are a separate list.
crops.types: Noble, Carlos, Southern Home, Black Beauty. Bunch grapes: Blanc Du Bois, Conquistador, Black Spanish.

crops.name: Persimmon
crops.types: Fuyu, Tanenashi, Saijo.

crops.name: Low-chill peach and nectarine
crops.types: Peach: Flordaprince, TropicBeauty, UFSun. Nectarine: Sunraycer, Sunbest.

crops.name: Cold-hardy avocado
crops.note: March, once frost danger has passed. Protected coastal spots.
crops.types: Duke, Mexicola, Winter Mexican. The dooryard guide calls these the cold-hardy choices for central Florida.

crops.name: Loquat
crops.note: March. Most other tropicals in that table are for south Florida.
crops.types: Wolfe, Oliver, Tanaka.

varietyNote: Variety names are the ones those Florida guides list. The page shortens long tables. It does not add cultivars from national catalogs.
